name: ParametricNoise spectral shape and phase scramble
plain: SpectralShape multiplies the 2-D FFT of the noise by a radial power-law tilt and an optional soft-edged band filter (low, high, band pass or notch), zeroes DC, and renormalizes per channel. The band edges use an erf ramp instead of a hard cut to avoid ringing. PhaseScramble keeps an amplitude spectrum and swaps in a new phase: either a random phase taken from the FFT of a fresh Gaussian field (so the result stays real), or, with a second noise wired, that noise's amplitude with this noise's phase; strength blends the complex spectra.
math:
Symbols: F=fft2(x); r radial frequency normalised to 1 at each axis Nyquist; α tilt; S(r,c,w)=½(1+erf((r−c)/(w√2))).
Shape: G(r)=r^(−α/2)·band(r); band = 1−S(r,hi) (low), S(r,lo) (high), S(r,lo)(1−S(r,hi)) (band), 1−that (notch); G(0)=0. out=N(Re ifft2(F·G)).
Scramble: φ=angle(fft2(z)), z fresh N(0,I); F'=|F|e^{iφ} (or |fft2(b)|e^{i·angle F}); out=N(Re ifft2((1−s)F + sF')).

props.params: alpha 0 (−3..3), mode power_law|low_pass|high_pass|band_pass|notch, low_cut 0.1, high_cut 0.5, falloff 0.1; scramble strength 1.0
